_note: 원문 유형은 글의 순서. order를 가장 강하게 구성하고, 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다.

passage: A language is culture made audible.
As children move through the stages of acquisition, they absorb more than vocabulary and grammar.
What they take in are the interaction styles that make them effective speakers in each setting.
In individualistic societies that style is direct, favoring categorical words such as absolutely or certainly.
In collectivistic societies, values of interdependence and harmony pull speech toward maybe or perhaps.
English alone among the world's languages capitalizes the pronoun for the self.
Japanese, by contrast, offers no single equivalent of that pronoun.
The word for the self shifts with situation, gender, age, and the listener's standing.
choices: why English grammar is harder to learn than Japanese grammar
how children memorize new vocabulary at each stage of development
how culture shapes the communication styles that children acquire
why capital letters were introduced into European writing systems
how bilingual speakers switch between two languages in conversation
theme.explanation_ko: 아이들이 습득하는 의사소통 방식이 문화에 따라 직접적·간접적으로 갈린다는 내용. ③이 주제.
theme.distractor_ko: ①문법 난이도, ②어휘 암기, ④대문자의 역사, ⑤이중언어 전환은 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: We should stop treating language learning as the mastery of words alone.
Children in every culture absorb the interaction styles that surround them.
Those styles decide whether a speaker sounds competent in a given situation.
A direct culture teaches its children to say absolutely and certainly without hesitation.
A culture built on interdependence teaches them to soften claims with maybe or perhaps.
We must therefore read a speaker's vagueness as a cultural habit, not a personal flaw.
English capitalizes the pronoun for the self, while Japanese has no fixed equivalent at all.
Judging one style by the standards of the other misreads both.
choices: 언어 교육은 어휘와 문법 암기에 집중해야 한다.
모호한 화법은 개인의 결함이므로 교정해야 한다.
영어의 대문자 표기는 다른 언어에도 도입되어야 한다.
화법의 직접성·간접성은 문화적 습관으로 이해해야 한다.
아이들은 성인이 된 뒤에야 의사소통 방식을 익힌다.
claim.explanation_ko: 직접적이든 간접적이든 화법은 문화가 가르친 습관이므로 그 기준으로 이해해야 한다는 주장. ④.
claim.distractor_ko: ①암기 중심, ②개인 결함론, ③대문자 도입, ⑤성인기 습득은 본문 주장이 아니다.

passage: Language is one of the clearest ways a culture reveals itself.
Children learn not the language itself but the ways of using it that a situation demands.
The style they build is specific to their culture.
Individualistic cultures produce direct, explicit speech with categorical words.
Collectivistic cultures, valuing harmony, produce implicit and even ambiguous speech.
English is the world's only language that writes the self with a capital letter.
Japanese has no single word matching that pronoun.
Its speakers choose among many self-terms according to situation and listener.
choices: 언어 습득은 나이가 어릴수록 빠르게 이루어진다.
아이들은 문화에 따라 직접적이거나 간접적인 의사소통 방식을 익힌다.
대명사 체계가 복잡한 언어일수록 배우기 어렵다.
집단주의 문화에서는 언어 교육이 늦게 시작된다.
모호한 표현은 어느 문화에서나 의사소통을 방해한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 문화에 따라 직접적·간접적 의사소통 방식을 익힌다는 것이 요지. ②.
gist.distractor_ko: ①습득 속도, ③학습 난이도, ④교육 시기, ⑤모호함의 폐해는 요지가 아니다.

passage: Every language carries the shape of the culture that speaks it.
Children acquire, above all, the interaction styles their situations call for.
Those styles differ sharply between individualistic and collectivistic societies.
One favors absolutely and certainly; the other favors maybe and perhaps.
Harmony and interdependence make vagueness a virtue rather than a fault.
English writes the self with a capital letter, alone among world languages.
Japanese has no fixed counterpart for that pronoun at all.
There, the word for the self bends to situation, age, gender, and listener.
choices: Why Capital Letters Matter in Modern Writing
The Fastest Way to Teach Children New Words
One Grammar, Many Nations: A Study of English
Absolutely or Perhaps: How Culture Teaches Us to Speak
The Decline of Formal Pronouns Around the World
title.explanation_ko: absolutely(직접)와 perhaps(간접)를 대비해 문화가 화법을 가르친다는 내용을 압축한 ④가 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①대문자 중요성, ②어휘 교수법, ③영어 문법 연구, ⑤경어 대명사의 쇠퇴는 초점이 아니다.

passage: Language is a manifestation of the culture that produced it.
Children pick up not words alone but the styles of interaction around them.
In individualistic cultures those styles run direct and explicit.
In collectivistic cultures, harmony asks speakers to leave the door half open.
So maybe and perhaps replace absolutely and certainly.
English, uniquely, spells the self with a capital letter.
Japanese offers no single equivalent for that pronoun.
Its self-terms shift with situation, gender, age, and listener.
choices: speak so quietly that others cannot hear
refuse to take part in the conversation
state a claim without closing off other possibilities
end a discussion before agreement is reached
repeat the listener's words back to them
implication.explanation_ko: '문을 반쯤 열어 둔다'는 비유는 단정하지 않고 다른 가능성을 남겨 두는 화법을 뜻한다. 뒤 문장의 maybe·perhaps와 호응한다. ③.
implication.distractor_ko: ①작은 목소리, ②대화 거부, ④대화 종료, ⑤반복은 모두 다르다.

passage: Language is a manifestation of culture.
Children learn the patterns of language interaction that enable them to function as competent communicators.
They develop a culture-specific style that is direct and explicit in individualistic cultures.
Examples of words linked with the direct style is categorical words like absolutely or certainly.

passage: Language is a manifestation of the culture behind it.

vocab.distractor_ko: ①발현 ②명시적인 ③단정적인 ⑤등가어는 문맥상 모두 적절하다.

order.given: Language is a manifestation of culture, and children acquire not language itself but the interaction styles that make them competent communicators.

blocks.A: That convention may reflect the English roots of individualism, for Japanese offers no single equivalent and lets situation, age, and gender decide which self-term is used.
blocks.B: By contrast, collectivistic assumptions of interdependence and harmony keep speakers to implicit, even ambiguous terms such as maybe or perhaps, and English remains the only language that spells the self with a capital letter.
blocks.C: The style they build is culture-specific, running direct and explicit in individualistic societies, where categorical words like absolutely and certainly are typical.

order.explanation_ko: (C)의 They가 주어진 글의 children을 받고, (B)의 By contrast가 (C)의 직접적 화법과 대조되며, (A)의 That convention이 (B) 끝의 '대문자 I' 관습을 받는다. (C)-(B)-(A).
order.distractor_ko: (B)의 By contrast는 대조할 앞 내용이 필요하고, (A)의 That convention은 대문자 표기가 먼저 언급되어야만 가리킬 대상이 생긴다.

summary.summary_template: Because language expresses culture, children in individualistic societies learn a __(A)__ style, while those in collectivistic societies learn one that is __(B)__ .

writing.en_prompt: They develop a culture-specific communication style that is, for example, direct and explicit in individualistic cultures or indirect and implicit in collectivistic cultures.
writing.answer: 그들은 문화 특유의 의사소통 방식을 발달시키는데, 예를 들어 개인주의 문화에서는 직접적이고 명시적이며 집단주의 문화에서는 간접적이고 암시적인 방식이다.

writing.question: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 한 단어를 각각 쓰시오.
